name: Svartsö
description: Svartsö is a long but easy SAT island section: a roughly 17.9 km figure-eight of gravel/compacted roads and local forest/path sections through open grazing landscapes, lakes, villages and several ferry-access spurs. It can be started from Norra Svartsö, Alsvik, Skälvik or Söderboudd, so present it as a multi-access loop network rather than a single-start trail. Alsvik is the main service cluster, with seasonal public toilet/water at the guest harbour and food/shop options nearby; Norra Svartsö adds a private-hosted off-season toilet/water fallback at the hotel. Many other amenities are seasonal, paid, customer-only or private.
utilities: Confirmed seasonal public toilet at Alsvik guest harbour; SAT says it is not available in winter.
Confirmed seasonal public water at Alsvik guest harbour; do not expose lakes as drinking-water taps.

Private-hosted/year-round toilet and water fallback at Svartsö Skärgårdshotell near Norra Svartsö is supported by SAT winter/off-season guidance; verify before relying and do not treat hotel showers/guest amenities as public.
Svartsö Lanthandel, café, Svartsö Krog and Bistro Sågen are confirmed food/shop/service candidates, but opening hours vary by season and customer/booking caveats apply.
No official campsite or public hiker shelter confirmed.
No official public fireplace/firepit confirmed; one grill candidate near Sågens brygga remains pending/suppressed until stronger source confirms public use.
Waste should default to pack-out guidance. Svartsö ÅVC and harbor waste/miljöstation references are not normal trail-litter bins and need caveats.
The four ferry-quay transit pins duplicate access metadata. During integration, render ferry stops from access metadata or use transit facilities as fallback, not both.
waterSources: Use Alsvik guest harbour as the strongest confirmed public water refill point, seasonal and not in winter.
Svartsö Skärgårdshotell near Norra Svartsö is a private-hosted/year-round water fallback per SAT winter/off-season guidance; verify before relying.
Do not expose Storträsket, Lillträsket or other lakes as drinking water. SAT describes Storträsket as the island drinking-water source, not a public tap.
Restaurants/shop may provide water or toilets for guests/customers, but do not model those as unconditional public refill points without confirmation.
notes: Route shape: multi-access figure-eight / loop network with ferry-spur options across Svartsö.
Model Svartsö as a multi-access figure-eight/loop network with four ferry quays, not a simple single trailhead loop.
Alsvik is the main public service cluster; guest-harbour toilet/water are seasonal and not in winter.

Norra Svartsö/Skärgårdshotellet provides a private-hosted off-season toilet/water fallback and defibrillator per SAT, but verify before relying and do not treat hotel showers/sauna/lodging as public facilities.
Use opening-hours and customer/guest caveats for food, lodging, sauna, showers and restaurant toilets.

No organized campsite is confirmed. Local Hembygdsgården tenting references are allemansrätten context only: small, discreet, short stay, away from homes, crops and active pasture, with local permission/verification where needed. Do not convert this into a campsite facility.
Ferry waiting shelters at quays, if later mapped, are transit comfort only and not hiker shelters.
Render ferry stops from accessMetadataDraft as the primary access layer; keep transit facilities only as fallback if the app cannot consume access metadata. Never render both layers at once.
Keep dogs controlled/leashed near livestock and wildlife, especially March 1-August 20 and around grazing animals.
Close gates, stay on roads/marked paths through pasture and respect private houses, fields and crops.
Do not expose lakes as potable water. Storträsket is described as an island drinking-water source, not a public tap.
Treat Alsvik/Hembygdsgården as one bathing cluster with Naturkartan source aliases and no official HaV sampled-water-quality status unless later verified.
Keep Lillträsket and route-wide grazing landscape context in description/notes rather than precise map pins unless later integration supports scenic micro-POIs or route-wide context markers.
Keep defibrillators as guarded emergency metadata, not attraction POIs or ordinary trail facilities.
Use live SL/Waxholmsbolaget planning because request stops, booking symbols, summer timetable updates and ticket validity matter.

facilities.name: Public toilet at Alsvik guest harbour
facilities.description: Public toilet at Alsvik guest harbour, the main service cluster for the Svartsö section. Seasonal: SAT says no toilet/water here in winter.

facilities.name: Water at Alsvik guest harbour
facilities.description: Confirmed public water refill point at Alsvik guest harbour, seasonal and not island-wide tap coverage.

facilities.name: Svartsö Lanthandel
facilities.description: Year-round grocery/general store at Alsvik with café and practical services. Opening hours vary by season and can exclude Sundays; verify current hours before relying on it. Do not model any paid/inside-store toilet as an unconditional public toilet.

facilities.name: Svartsö bryggcafé / café at Lanthandeln
facilities.description: Café service in the Alsvik/Lanthandel cluster. Treat as opening-hours dependent.

facilities.name: Svartsö Krog
facilities.description: Restaurant east of Alsvik on or near the route. Confirm current opening hours and booking before relying on it.

facilities.name: Bistro Sågen
facilities.description: Restaurant near the central/southern SAT route. SAT step guide says it is 500-600 m south of the four-way intersection and worth visiting; verify opening hours and booking before relying on it.

facilities.name: Alsvik / Hembygdsgården bathing area
facilities.description: Alsvik/Hembygdsgården bathing cluster. Naturkartan lists two very nearby Svartsö bathing entries, and local/Värmdö island material says bathing is available by Hembygdsgården. Treat as one swimming facility unless later map work proves separate maintained spots; no official HaV sampled-water-quality status found.

facilities.name: Svartsö Skärgårdshotell year-round toilet
facilities.description: Year-round toilet fallback near Norra Svartsö from SAT winter/off-season guidance. Treat as private-hosted and verify-before-relying, not a municipal public toilet.

facilities.name: Water at Svartsö Skärgårdshotell
facilities.description: Year-round water fallback near Norra Svartsö from SAT winter/off-season guidance. Use as a caveated fallback, not as an unconditional public tap.

facilities.name: Norra Svartsö ferry quay
facilities.description: Northern ferry access point and one valid start for the Svartsö SAT network. Winter service can be limited when ice is not broken on the north side.

facilities.name: Alsvik/Ahlsvik ferry quay
facilities.description: Most service-rich ferry access point, by shop/café/guest harbour. Served by Waxholmsbolaget line 13; local page says Waxholmsbolaget serves it year-round and Cinderella seasonally.

facilities.name: Skälvik ferry quay
facilities.description: Southern ferry access point. SAT says hikers arriving at Skälvik follow gravel road north about 700 m to rejoin the route.

facilities.name: Söderboudd ferry quay
facilities.description: Eastern/southern ferry access point. Useful for shorter linear variants or exits after the east loop.

facilities.name: Storträsket and Boholmen
facilities.description: Svartsö's largest lake and a scenic heritage/nature context. SAT describes Storträsket as the island's drinking-water source, and local/Värmdö sources say residents around the lakes take drinking water from them; this is not a public water refill point. Boholmen in Storträsket is linked to stories from the 1719 Russian ravages, when islanders hid there with their possessions.

facilities.name: Svartsö Hembygdsgården / former mission house
facilities.description: Former mission house near Alsvik, inaugurated in 1880 and now used as Svartsö's community/heritage building. Local sources mention tenting by Hembygdsgården under allemansrätten, but there is no organized campsite on the island, so do not map it as a campsite or rest area.

facilities.name: Stenhuset in Alsvik
facilities.description: Privately owned stone manor/heritage house in Alsvik, built in 1732 and identified by RAÄ as having high cultural-historical value. Present as view-from-road heritage context only; do not imply public courtyard or interior access.
